title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-burst-reporting-enhancement
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Enhances Dedicated autoscaler with priority-aware routing and expanded burst/utilization reporting. Adds new metrics (burst_utilization, token_bucket_fill, burst_queue_depth), dashboard, and config options for smoothing and priority weights. Backwards compatible.
description: Context: Customers running high-variance workloads on Dedicated fleets observed repeated aggressive scale-ups during short traffic spikes which both increased cost and created noisy autoscaler activity. This PR introduces priority-aware routing in the autoscaler and richer burst/utilization telemetry so platform teams can target smoothing and throughput guarantees per-customer tier. Summary of changes: - Add priority routing hooks so requests tagged with a priority label route through a token-bucket queue that respects reserved throughput for high-priority tenants. - Expose new metrics: burst_utilization, token_bucket_fill, burst_queue_depth, priority_throughput_ratio. - Add token-bucket smoothing tuning parameters (smoothing_window_ms, decay_factor) and safer defaults to reduce oscillation. - Add dedicated dashboard and alerting examples for burst behavior. - Add migration code to preserve existing configs and a small schema bump. - Include unit and e2e tests + performance benchmark harness. Checklist: - [x] Design review (ENG-431) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration/e2e tests added - [x] Benchmarks and perf numbers included - [x] Docs updated (autoscaler config + dashboard) Motivation and impact: This is intended to reduce cost and scale churn during transient spikes while preserving throughput guarantees for premium customers. Benchmarks (see commits) show ~12% reduction in 95th-tail latency during bursts and ~18% fewer scale-up events in mixed-priority workloads. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless new priority config is set. Rollout plan: staged rollout to Dedicated fleets using canary policy in the Console with automatic rollback on increased error rate.

review_conversation: Miguel Torres (reviewer): Left a comment asking about cardinality impact of new metrics; suggested tagging metrics with priority level only and avoid per-tenant dimensions by default.

Priya Patel (author): Responded that metrics are emitted with priority_cardinality low by default; added metric labels annotation and adjusted exports to limit cardinality. Updated code to emit tenant_id only under debug flag.
Anika Bose (reviewer): Requested additional e2e scenarios to validate fallback when token bucket is exhausted and suggested tuning decay_factor default to 0.9 to reduce oscillation.
Priya Patel (author): Added e2e test 'burst_priority_fallback' and adjusted default decay_factor to 0.92 based on benchmark runs; pushed new commit.

Daniel Kim (reviewer): Asked for migration plan and how config bump is handled during rolling upgrades. Priya added migration docs and a safe-check in the controller to treat missing fields as defaults.
CI: integration-tests flaky on first run (TestAutoscalerBurstSuite) — reran and passed. Reviewers re-approved after fixes.
Miguel Torres: Approved. Anika Bose: Approved. Daniel Kim: Approved.
merge_summary: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI. Included perf report and dashboard assets. Deployed to canary fleets via release pipeline.
notes: This change is low-risk when using defaults but enables operators to fine-tune smoothing and reserved throughput per-priority. Watch burst_utilization and burst_queue_depth during canary rollout; alerts provided in the dashboard example.
perf_results: local/benchmarks: mixed-priority workload (1000 hosts): 12% decrease in p95 latency during bursts, 18% fewer autoscaler scale-ups, median CPU unchanged. Full bench report attached in commits.
migration_steps: 1) Update autoscaler config schema will be automatically applied at controller startup. 2) Existing configs without priority settings will keep previous behavior. 3) To opt-in: set priority_weights and smoothing_window_ms in dedicated autoscaler values.yaml. 4) Roll out to canary fleet, monitor burst_utilization metric and alerts.
